items.title: Press play on Elastic Security 9.6, banger after banger
items.summary: AlertZero works your alert queue in the background and nothing consequential it proposes runs until you approve it. 9.6 also brings entity resolution, MITRE ATLAS mappings, 143 AI detection rules, and Linux ransomware protection.

items.title: AlertZero in Elastic Security: Every alert answered. Every decision yours
items.summary: Agents triage alerts, hunt threats, tune noisy rules and reconstruct what happened on a host. Each hands you a proposed action with the evidence behind it, and you set how far it goes alone and which model it uses.

items.title: Elastic ships 143 detection rules for AI agents and LLM platforms
items.summary: A fake MCP server copied every outgoing email to an attacker and the new rules catch that, along with coding agents running attacker commands, secrets pasted into prompts, and stolen keys running models on your bill.

items.title: Thinking fast about prompt injection: New System 1 models in Elastic
items.summary: Four small classifiers score every GenAI prompt and response at ingest, inside your own cluster, catching prompt injection, encoded payloads, obfuscated words and refusals without an LLM reading every event.

items.title: Mapping the AI threat landscape: MITRE ATLAS comes to Elastic Security
items.summary: Elastic Security 9.6 adds MITRE ATLAS to our detection rules and the tools you use to manage them, so you can see which AI attacks your rules already cover.

items.title: From posture to root cause: Investigate OpenShift compliance with Elastic Agent Builder
items.summary: When an OpenShift compliance control fails, Elastic Agent Builder traces the root cause, from Compliance Operator scans centralized in Elasticsearch and CEL checks for the rules the scanner marks manual.

items.title: We caught the agent-framework PyPI compromise six minutes after it published
items.summary: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 stole Azure, Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions tokens from a .pth hook that ran on every Python launch, so if either one touched a build agent or a laptop, assume every secret on that host is gone.

items.title: Inside the loop: Five AI attack frameworks that never ask permission
items.summary: Five agentic offensive frameworks act in bursts of two to 25 seconds, and none enforces authorization in code. What ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, Cairn, PentAGI, and HexStrike leave in your telemetry, and the ES|QL hunt that catches them.

items.title: 56 AWS API calls in 141 milliseconds: Inside an AI-run intrusion
items.summary: A CyberStrikeAI server spent 16 days in four AWS accounts using eight identities, and the CloudTrail record shows why six detection rules each caught only part of it.

items.title: 0% GPU utilization: How SANSAR hides Linux cryptomining
items.summary: Elastic Security Labs analyzes SANSAR, a Linux cryptomining orchestrator that manages miners over Tor, alongside a kernel rootkit, GPU monitoring hooks and a backdoor that retrieves its C2 address from Ethereum.

items.title: Modernising threat hunting: Using Semantic Search to Find Risky AI Agent Behavior
items.summary: I tested vector search on 7,454 turns of my own agent sessions. One in seven sessions needed review, the agent’s reasoning carried more signal than the prompt, and the stored vectors answer questions nobody thought to ask at ingest.

items.title: When trust becomes the payload: Inside the threats, etc quarterly report
items.summary: The newest threats, etc report details how adversaries are weaponizing trust across the entire enterprise stack, abusing everything from AI assistants and npm supply chains to identity flows and legitimate management tools.
